newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't will appeal labor decree setback.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't will appeal labor decree setback.

text.p: The Argentine government will appeal a court decision annulling President Carlos Menem's unpopular labor reform decrees, Labor Minister Armando Caro Figueroa said a few hours after the ruling Tuesday.

He told a news conference that Labor Judge Ines Gassibe's ruling of "non-applicability", following her suspension of the three decrees last week pending a government explanation, "did not convince the executive power and after a long, careful analysis we have decided to appeal the sentence."
Judge Gassibe froze the decrees on a petition from the CGT trade union federation, following a ruling by another labor judge earlier this month that the decrees violated the Argentine constitution.

Her ruling says the constitution "consecrates unions' guaranteed right to arrange collective labor agreements." Overturning such rights by decree also violates norms of the Geneva-based International Labor Organization, Gassibe said.

Menem's decrees would let smaller firms bypass national unions in collective pay talks and let firms appeal to the government if they want to negotiate with trade unions on a company-by-company and not an industry-wide basis.

Arguing that "flexibilization" of labor is the best way to tackle 17.3 percent unemployment, Menem resorted to decrees in the face of Congress opposition and a breakdown in talks with unions, who fear their power is under threat.
The CGT staged a 24-hour general strike on December 26, its third in the year.
The Peronist government at first threatened to impeach the 77-year-old Labor Judge Julio Garcia Martinez who incurred its wrath by ruling the decrees unconstitutional.

But Caro Figueroa tried to tone down the debate by making it clear that there would be no attempt to impeach Gassibe, and that if the higher courts reject its appeals it will comply with their decisions.

"What is sure and certain is that the government will appeal this sentence. When we have a case open we try all appeal routes possible. But if the final ruling is adverse, we accept it," said the minister.
